children: Australia's next federal election appears set to have the issue of immigration at center stage. The right-wing One Nation Party, which is expected garner significant support at the poll due by May 2028, has pledged to slash the number of temporary visa holders and unlawful non-citizens in the country by more than 750,000 over three years if it wins power. The plan will restore living standards, ease pressure on housing and essential services and bring population growth back to a sustainable rate, the party's leader Pauline Hanson says. "Australians have had enough of mass migration and have been heard loud and clear," she adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
